name: Sit to stand
movement: standing up from a chair without the hands and sitting back down slowly

phone.placement: Stand the phone up on the floor, two or three metres away, side on to the chair.

words.hint: From a firm chair: stand up without using the hands, then sit back down slowly.
words.start: Stand the phone up on the floor. Sit on the front half of a firm chair, side on to it, feet flat and arms folded.
words.position: Sit on the front half of a firm chair, side on to the phone, feet flat and a little back under the knees, arms folded across the chest.
words.top: Standing fully upright — knees and hips straight, the trunk tall — before sitting back down under control.
howto: Sit toward the front of a firm chair, feet flat, hip-width and just behind the knees, arms folded across your chest.
Lean forward — nose over toes — and stand up, pushing through the whole foot, without using your hands.
Stand all the way up, tall, and hold for the count.
Sit back down slowly, over three seconds, reaching the hips back to the seat. The rep counts when you are sitting.
words.cannot: How much the hands or the momentum help: it sees the knee straightening, the trunk at the top and the shins. Keep the arms folded yourself.
words.about: Sit to stand — side on to the chair: the knee angle, from about 90 sitting; a rep is under way past 140 and counts once the knee is back under 110 on the seat; at the top at least 165° — standing fully up; the trunk at the top within 15° of upright; the feet, while sitting, just behind the knees (the shin at least 85° from the floor); and the heels down, read against the start. Hold one second standing, sit over three. A quick test of leg strength and the most useful exercise for stairs and getting about.
words.lost: Sit side on to the camera, the whole body in
words.early: Stand all the way up next time
words.safety: A firm chair that will not slide. Use the hands if you need them, and a higher seat makes it easier.
words.easier: A higher seat or a cushion; a hand on the thigh; fewer reps.
words.harder: A lower seat; a slower sit; a weight held at the chest; one leg doing more.
words.mistakes: Pushing off with the hands; rocking to get up; dropping into the seat; not standing fully upright; heels lifting; feet too far forward; knees caving inward.

measurements.label: knee straight
measurements.why: The knee angle: about 90 sitting, 180 standing. Also the progress measurement: under way past raiseAt, sitting again under downAt.

settings.label: Knee angle standing, at least (180 is straight)

measurements.label: trunk at the top
measurements.why: The trunk off vertical, + forward. Leaning forward is right on the way up; at the top the body should be tall.

settings.label: Trunk within ± of upright at the top (degrees)

measurements.label: shin from the floor
measurements.why: The ankle-to-knee line from the floor, judged sitting: 90 is the shin upright, more the feet tucked behind the knees. Under 85 the feet are out in front, which makes standing harder on the knees and the back.

settings.label: Shin angle from the floor, at least

measurements.label: heels down

settings.label: Heel lifted, at most (degrees from the start)

measurements.why: The heel against the toe, as the change since the start: rising onto the toes to stand reads up.

faults.label: Heels lifting
faults.text: Heels down — push through the whole foot

faults.label: Not fully up
faults.text: Stand all the way up — straighten the knees

faults.label: Feet too far forward
faults.text: Feet back a little — just behind the knees

settings.label: Knee angle that counts as under way
